#
#    pip-compile --output-file=requirements.txt requirements.in
#
# HAND-EDITED AFTERWARDS -- five pins, deliberately, do not let a recompile drop them
# without regenerating tests/regression/baselines/ in the same breath:
#
#     joblib 1.5.1 -> 1.5.2      llvmlite 0.44.0 -> 0.45.1    numba 0.61.2 -> 0.62.1
#     scikit-learn 1.7.1 -> 1.7.2                             scipy 1.12.0 -> 1.17.1
#
# Why (measured 2026-09-05, the first time CI ever ran tests/regression): the numerical
# baselines were generated on the maintainer's environment, which had drifted off this
# lockfile. Installed faithfully from the OLD pins, 10 of 14 regression tests failed --
# and not by rounding. HDBSCAN found 4 clusters instead of 3, the adjusted Rand index
# against the baseline clustering was 0.21 against a floor of 0.95, and every downstream
# score shifted (target_0_Mean_Score -0.3554 -> -0.4272). The embedding itself was only
# slightly perturbed (pairwise-distance correlation 0.994), which is the signature of a
# small numerical change crossing a clustering decision boundary and being amplified.
#
# Mechanism: UMAP's core is numba-JIT compiled, so a numba/llvmlite bump changes
# floating-point codegen. Ruled out by measurement, not assumption -- the same suite
# passes 14/14 locally when pinned to 4 cores, so thread count is NOT the cause.
#
# These five versions are not a guess: they are the combination the baselines were
# actually validated against and which is proven to coexist. Changing them means
# regenerating the baselines (`pytest tests/regression --regen-baselines`), which
# changes what the numerical pinning asserts -- a scientific decision, not a chore.
#
# A proper `pip-compile` under Python 3.11 (this file says 3.12, while CI and the dev
# environment both run 3.11) is still owed; see STATUS.md.
#
